clue.text: Superficial justice

definitions.meaning: lacking depth, not deep in thought or feeling
Justice ... is the foolish country magistrate in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2 and The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.walkthrough: The lower-case 'justice' hides a title: it is the Shakespearean JP, not the abstract virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: lacking depth is the everyday adjective, and the name belongs to Shakespeare's comic rural magistrate.

clue.text: Maroon thread

definitions.meaning: to leave someone ..., as on a desert island

explanation.definitionFit: Maroon is a verb meaning to abandon, matching the verb sense, while the noun is a single fibre or filament.

clue.text: A ship, for instance — first-class fighting implement

parts.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship
eg is short for exempli gratia, for example
A1 is first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: A first-class battleship given as an example of a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, Lloyd's register's top rating, is written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used by southern African warriors, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: With an old guinea, head for country scenery

parts.note: a guinea was one pound one shilling, abbreviated L for pound and S for shilling
and means with
S is the shilling part of the old guinea
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: Instructions to take a guinea and set off to the rural landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: The guinea, a pre-decimal British coin, was worth one pound and one shilling (L and S), so AND (with) goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a view of rural scenery, or a painting of one.

clue.text: Rig the crew and I reorganized

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new arrangement, as a crew might be reorganized

explanation.surface: Fitting out a boat and rearranging its crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rig' suggests a ship's rigging, but it means an outfit: a windcheater is a windproof jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Rig is informal for clothing or outfit, and a windproof jacket is an item of such gear.

clue.text: A girl of the country

parts.note: France is a country
'of the country' is the possessive, written with apostrophe-s

explanation.surface: A young woman who comes from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the country' reads as rural, but it is FRANCE'S, belonging to France; drop the apostrophe for the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Frances is a woman's given name, so it names a girl.

clue.text: Pay for an unfinished meal

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for meal is cut off

parts.note: a feed is a meal

explanation.surface: Paying for a meal left half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final D of FEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee is a payment for a service.

clue.text: So that one can hear and let hear

indicators.note: to hear is to listen, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: allowed means let, permitted

explanation.surface: Speak up, so that someone can hear, and let them hear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' turns ALLOWED (let) into its homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking audibly means speaking out at a volume others can catch.

clue.text: Shut down a big picture

definitions.meaning: to ... a shop is to shut it
a photograph or film shot taken very near

explanation.definitionFit: To close up a premises is to shut it, and the noun is a photo filling the frame with its subject.

clue.text: Sprinklers collect on board

indicators.note: on board a ship means held within its letters

parts.note: a ship is boarded, SS being a steamship
a collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy

explanation.surface: Gathering garden watering cans on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means inside SS, the steamship. 'collect' is the noun, a church prayer, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprayers are devices that scatter fine droplets, as sprinklers do.

clue.text: Horse one trains to tumble

indicators.note: tumbling throws the letters of 'one trains' into a new order

explanation.surface: A racehorse that one trains is made to take a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tumble' rearranges ONETRAINS. Rosinante is Don Quixote's bony old nag in Cervantes's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosinante is the famous steed of Don Quixote, and the name is used for any old worn-out mount.

clue.text: Produced by incense when Bishop visits old city

indicators.note: the bishop arrives at the city, so his name sits right up against its name

parts.note: Odo was the Norman bishop of Bayeux, half-brother of William the Conqueror
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Incense drifts through the air as a bishop calls on an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop Odo of Bayeux, William the Conqueror's half-brother, is a stock crossword bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning incense gives off a smell, a scent that fills the room.

clue.text: Top Abyssinian drink

definitions.meaning: the title of the emperor of Abyssinia, the old name for Ethiopia
a hot drink of port or sherry with sugar, lemon and spice

explanation.definitionFit: It is the Ethiopian royal title for the supreme ruler, and also an eighteenth-century mulled wine named after Colonel Francis Negus.

clue.text: Groceries — exclaim about the name

indicators.note: the shout goes round, so the word for the name sits inside it

parts.note: to exclaim is to cry out
a handle is slang for a person's name

explanation.surface: Someone shouting out the brand name of their shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groceries' is a shop's stock here; 'handle' for a name is informal, as in a CB radio handle, and 'about' puts it inside the shout.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandlery is a shop selling provisions and supplies, originally candles and ships' stores, so it is a grocery trade.

clue.text: Diplomatic bag?

parts.note: not the sealed official pouch but a document case such as an embassy official might carry

explanation.walkthrough: A diplomatic bag is official mail sent under protection; here it is a briefcase of the kind carried by an embassy staffer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim hard briefcase for papers, named after the embassy official.

clue.text: Weed put in it for burning

definitions.text: Weed put in it for burning

parts.words: Weed put in it for burning
parts.note: 'weed' is slang for tobacco; this thin sheet holds the tobacco while it is rolled and smoked

explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' suggests a garden bonfire, but it is tobacco rolled up for smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin sheets used to roll tobacco into a smoke that is then lit.

clue.text: Little boys get older, it's the custom

parts.note: Pat is a short form of Patrick
Ron is a short form of Ronald
to age is to get older

explanation.surface: Small sons growing up, as is the tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortened names (Pat, Ron) are the 'little' boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom is regular business from customers, which is patronage.

clue.text: In Paris I became objective with an Italian delicacy

indicators.note: the subject pronoun is swapped for its objective-case form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller in Paris turning dispassionate about Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: In the word 'Paris' the letter I is changed to ME, its objective form, giving PARMES; then add AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese prized as a fine food.

clue.text: Article that I continue changing and verifying

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: changing the order of the letters of 'that I continue' gives a new word

explanation.surface: A newspaper article that someone keeps altering while checking the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like the newspaper sense, but it is the grammatical one; 'changing' shuffles the remaining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentication is the act of checking that something is genuine, which is what verifying means.

clue.text: Paddy, takes so much French drink

parts.note: tant is French for so much
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: An Irishman drinking a lot of French booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman but is a British informal word for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is a fit of temper, a childish outburst.

clue.text: Instrument means nothing to 'empress lacking last letter

parts.note: O looks like a zero

indicators.note: Z, the final letter of the alphabet, is dropped

parts.note: a czarina is a Russian empress

explanation.surface: An instrument that means nothing to an empress short of a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'last letter' is Z, of the alphabet, not the last letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument.

clue.text: Sort of ring up several soldiers?

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading up means backwards

parts.note: ten taken as an indefinite number
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Ringing up a number of soldiers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TENGIS, read from the bottom of a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet ring carries a seal engraved on it.

clue.text: Where to see animals and people by Silver Lake

parts.note: men means people
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Lake Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A guide to spotting wildlife and crowds beside a place called Silver Lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for display, like a small zoo.

clue.text: Bettin' Arab

definitions.meaning: gambling, with the final g dropped as in 'bettin''
street arab, an old term for a homeless urchin

explanation.walkthrough: Gaming with its g clipped, as 'bettin'' is clipped; 'street Arab' is a dated term for an urchin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dropped-g form of gambling, and a street urchin.

clue.text: Animal featuring in this book, a pig

indicators.note: the run of letters is found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Children's picture book with an animal in it, namely a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'bOOK A PIg'.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African forest mammal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: A watery liquid is all around 'er

indicators.note: the word for all goes round, enclosing the letters for her

parts.note: the sum is the whole, all of it
'er is her with the h dropped, written ER

explanation.surface: A remark that some watery liquid is spread all about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'er marks a dropped h, a convention for cockney speech; 'around' wraps the total about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Serum is the clear watery fluid left when blood clots, so it is a thin bodily liquid.

clue.text: What issues turned me against a lot of people?

indicators.note: placed up against, next to the following words
the word me is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a nation is a large body of people

explanation.surface: Asking what problems set someone against a great crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes EM from 'me'; 'issues' is a verb here, not the noun 'problems'.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that flows out from a source, as light or a smell comes forth.

clue.text: The first three of.27. wriggling fish

indicators.note: wriggling makes the letters squirm into another order
only the opening trio of letters of 27 Across is kept

parts.note: the answer to 27 Across

explanation.surface: Something wriggling, a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep ELE from 27 Across; 'wriggling' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a snakelike fish.

clue.text: No bird left, not in reality

parts.note: taken as written
mina, also spelt myna, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: No bird remains, which is not really the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal means existing in name only, as a nominal head who has no real power.

clue.text: The Spanish began it, losing their heads with grace

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'

indicators.note: both words lose their first letters, their heads

explanation.surface: Spanish speakers start something, gracefully lose their composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing their heads' takes the B from 'began' and the I from 'it', leaving EGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes someone or something stylish and graceful.
